title: Fund the best projects
prompt:
A small studio starts with funds and may complete at most k projects, one after another. Project i needs costs[i] in funds to start (the money is not spent) and adds profits[i] to the funds when it is done. Each project can be done once. Return the largest funds the studio can have after choosing projects well.

- 1 <= k <= 100,000 and 0 <= funds <= 10^9.
- profits and costs have the same length, 1 to 100,000, with values between 0 and 10^4 for profits and 0 to 10^9 for costs.
hints: At each step, among the projects you can afford right now, doing the most profitable one is never worse.
Funds only go up, so a project that becomes affordable stays affordable. Unlock projects in order of cost.
Keep the locked projects sorted (or in a min-heap) by cost, and the unlocked ones in a max-heap by profit.

solution.explanation: Two structures split the projects: those still too costly, ordered by cost, and those affordable, in a max-heap by profit. Each round moves every newly affordable project into the max-heap, then takes the most profitable. Picking the best affordable project is safe because profits only raise funds, which can only unlock more. If nothing is affordable, no later round can help, so stop early.

complexity.time: O(n log n + k log n)
complexity.notes: Sorting by cost is O(n log n); each project enters and leaves the max-heap at most once. A min-heap by cost instead of sorting gives the same bound.

followUps: Projects now spend their cost. How does the greedy choice change?
Return which projects were chosen, in order.
